The Renal Pathology Service at Hennepin County Medical Center (HCMC) provides complete laboratory services to support physicians in the diagnosis and management of kidney disease. To us, a complete set of services doesn’t just mean that we offer a full test menu and employ cutting-edge equipment and methodology.

It also means that we establish strong relationships with our clients through exceptional service and availability, as well as quick turnaround and easy access to results. Led by Gretchen S. Crary, MD, MBA, and a team of board-certified pathologists with experience and expertise in renal pathology, the Renal Pathology Service at HCMC is marked by our unmatched attention to detail, which ensures that each diagnosis is thorough and accurate. Look for dedicated support and definitive results from the organization that has been at the forefront of kidney disease for more than 40 years.

Tests Performed

We provide expert interpretation of native and transplant kidney biopsy specimens using:

light microscopy
immunofluorescence
electron microscopy
The results of these studies are integrated with the clinical presentation to provide a full and final interpretation of the patient’s renal disorder.

Reporting

Initial test results are usually available within 24 hours. Our pathologists provide consultation on all specimens by telephone.

Formal reports can be accessed through Aperio, our digital pathology site that we use to digitize and manage our slides. They can also be e-mailed, faxed, or mailed. Results from light microscopy and immunofluorescence tests are usually available within 1 day, with rush processing on request. Results from electron microscopy tests are typically available within 2 days.

DESCRIPTION:
The pathology team at Pharmaron includes clinical pathology, necropsy, histology and histopathology evaluation functions, meeting the GLP compliance requirements from FDA, OECD and CFDA.   The oversight of highly experienced pathologists is essential to evaluate both discovery and GLP histology and pathology specimens. Whether evaluating studies that are conducted in house, evaluating contract histopathology slides that are sent in, or performing peer review, our US Board Certified Veterinary pathologists provide the highest quality pathology interpretation and comprehensive report preparation. Our pathology reports include data acquired using FDA Part 11 compliant pathology data acquisition systems to collect and manage pathology data, thereby assuring the highest quality assessment and reporting of pathology data.

- Clinical pathology (clinical chemistry, hematology, coagulation and urinalysis)
- Necropsy with all species
- Histology
- Histopathology evaluation/diagnosis
- Comprehensive pathology reporting
- IND report preparation
- Validated, Part 11 compliant pathology data acquisition programs (Provantis®)
- GLP compliance in all phases
- Our state-of-the-art technology and extensive experience with biologics, antibodies, large molecules and small molecules enable us to offer a comprehensive and sophisticated pathologic assessments and interpretations. These and other specialty pathology services provide you with the most flexible, cost-effective, and timely product-specific resources possible.

DESCRIPTION:
A complete necropsy is performed. All organs are examined grossly, and the following organs are routinely weighed to the nearest milligram prior to fixation for determining organ-to-body weight ratios (percentage of body weight):

liver with gall bladder
spleen
kidneys (both) 
adrenals (both) 
heart 
lungs
ovaries/uterus or testes/epididymides 
thymus
Other organ(s) can be weighed based on the pathologist's recommendation or investigator's request.

Tissues are trimmed according to a standardized protocol, fixed in 10 percent neutral buffered formalin, processed by routine methods, embedded in paraffin wax, and sectioned at 4 microns for standard H&E.

Unstained and frozen sections can also be made.

All bony tissues are decalcified prior to trimming. Tissues are evaluated histologically by a comparative pathologist board-certified by the American College of Veterinary Pathologists. Final reports include an interpretative summary and recommendations for ancillary analyses offered by the CPMPSR or other Shared Resources.
